svg.title: “As a child . . . I listened to a lot of stories, moonlight stories told by the women in Ugwuta [Oguta]. . . . I would call on anybody who promised to tell me a story. . . . While I was teaching, I discovered I had plenty of time on my hands. . . . So, I began to write stories about my schooldays. It was in this process that I began the story of Efuru. It just happened. . . . There was nothing in me when I was in school that made me feel I was going to be a writer. . . . But having written Efuru and having published it, I continued to write.” — Flora Nwapa, in conversation with Marie Umeh, 1992
